incidents.victim: Government officials, military personnel, journalists and Ukraine-based officials
incidents.vector: Phishing messages impersonate messaging-app support accounts to trick high-value targets into surrendering verification codes, account PINs and backup recovery keys, enabling full account takeover of Signal, WhatsApp and Telegram accounts.
incidents.impact: Russian intelligence compromised individual messaging accounts (not the apps' encryption) to read private and group messages and steal sensitive military, political and economic information; a leaked backup recovery key stays valid even after the account is re-created. Disclosed jointly by FBI/CISA and Ukraine's SBU.

incidents.victim: John R. Bolton (former U.S. National Security Advisor)
incidents.vector: An Iran-linked cyber actor hacked Bolton's personal email account, which he had used to transmit and retain Top Secret/SCI material outside approved government systems.
incidents.impact: Bolton pleaded guilty to willfully retaining national defense information; DOJ says the compromised account held classified material on adversary military plans, covert U.S. actions and intelligence on foreign leaders, which the Iran-linked actor stole. Sentencing set for Oct 28.

incidents.victim: DraftKings (account holders)
incidents.vector: Credential-stuffing attack against user accounts, with access to compromised accounts resold via cybercriminal marketplaces.
incidents.impact: Roughly 68,000 accounts compromised in the 2022 attack; attackers added payment methods to about 1,600 accounts and stole around $600,000. Final defendant Nathan Austad sentenced to 18 months and $1.3M restitution.

incidents.victim: Ukrposhta (Ukraine's national postal operator)
incidents.vector: Overnight attack on the operator's IT systems; the group claims it breached infrastructure weeks earlier, accessed a server and exfiltrated a user database.
incidents.impact: Temporary disruption of Ukrposhta's mobile application. The 'IT Army of Russia' claimed responsibility and alleged prior data theft; the data-theft claim is unverified.

incidents.victim: Southeast Asian government entities and state-owned energy infrastructure
incidents.vector: Chinese-speaking actor exploited internet-facing web applications to drop ASPX web shells, then used SoftEther VPN, Mimikatz, JuicyPotato and a new bespoke .NET backdoor for persistence and exfiltration.
incidents.impact: Compromised at least ten organizations across Southeast Asia between September and December 2025, exfiltrating MSSQL database contents and web-server source code from government entities and breaching two state-owned critical energy infrastructure operators.

incidents.victim: Hospitality and hotel organizations in Europe and Asia
incidents.vector: Photo-themed ZIP archives delivered via phishing that routes through Calendly and Google redirect infrastructure (authentication laundering); fake image shortcut files launch obfuscated PowerShell that installs a Node.js implant with dual registry persistence.
incidents.impact: Active multi-stage intrusion campaign since April 2026 targeting front-desk and reservations staff, establishing persistent C2 access; investment in obfuscation and persistence suggests preparation for follow-on activity. Not attributed to a known actor.

incidents.victim: Fortinet, Sophos and Citrix VPN, RDP and MSSQL users worldwide
incidents.vector: Internet-wide mass scanning and password spraying that escalated to exploiting unpatched CVEs and a custom credential-sniffing script across 24 protocols; harvested hashes cracked on a GPU cluster. Australia's ACSC issued a critical alert.
incidents.impact: More than 74,000 leaked Fortinet device passwords (FortiBleed) found in an open directory; credentials validated and used to expand access inside victim networks and resold to other groups. Campaign began February 2026 and infrastructure remains active.

incidents.victim: Cisco Unified Communications Manager (CUCM) customers
incidents.vector: Active exploitation of CVE-2026-20230, an unauthenticated SSRF flaw in the WebDialer service chained to arbitrary file write, a JSP web shell and privilege escalation to root.
incidents.impact: Attackers weaponized a public proof-of-concept within 24 hours and began hitting CUCM systems on June 24, gaining root access. CUCM serves roughly 30M users across healthcare, finance, government and enterprise; orgs with WebDialer enabled are urged to assume compromise.

incidents.victim: Belgian State Security Service (VSSE)
incidents.vector: Data taken from a third-party company that managed the agency's mobile device management platform, linked to a series of attacks on Ivanti EPMM servers last year.
incidents.impact: Hackers stole names, phone numbers and email addresses of Belgian intelligence officials, exposing mobile-device details of intelligence personnel.

incidents.victim: Tata Electronics
incidents.vector: A data-extortion group listed Tata Electronics on its leak portal and claims theft of company documents.
incidents.impact: Tata Electronics confirmed a breach; the group claims to have stolen more than 200,000 documents allegedly containing sensitive data on Apple and Tesla electronic components.

incidents.victim: Ufagormolzavod (dairy producer, Russia)
incidents.vector: Cyberattack on the company's IT systems affecting logistics and accounting operations.
incidents.impact: Logistics and accounting disrupted, forcing manual processing of shipments; production not stopped. Part of a series of attacks on Russia's dairy sector, including a related website defacement with fabricated contamination claims.

incidents.victim: Service provider SD-WAN infrastructure (Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager)
incidents.vector: After gaining initial access via rogue peering and stolen certificate material, the actor exploited zero-day CVE-2026-20245 in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager via a malicious CSV upload to escalate to root, created a hidden root account, then ran extensive anti-forensic cleanup.
incidents.impact: Mandiant identified the intrusion at a service provider in early 2026; the actor exfiltrated SD-WAN fabric configurations and established stealthy, persistent control of the network's central control plane. Anti-forensic techniques minimized the investigative footprint.

incidents.victim: Transport for London, SSM Health and Sutter Health
incidents.vector: Voice and SMS phishing, SIM-swapping and help-desk social engineering to harvest credentials and MFA codes for network intrusions and ransomware.
incidents.impact: Two UK members of the 'Scattered Spider' group pleaded guilty to the August 2024 TfL attack; one also admitted hacking US healthcare providers SSM Health and Sutter Health. A related US indictment ties the group to 120 intrusions and over $115M in ransoms; sentencing July 15.

incidents.victim: Klue and its customers (including LastPass and Snyk)
incidents.vector: Attackers accessed market-intelligence platform Klue via a compromised legacy credential from a 2022 pilot, then stole customers' OAuth tokens and used them to download data from their Salesforce instances.
incidents.impact: At least eight companies confirmed Klue-related breaches, including LastPass and Snyk; a group calling itself 'Icarus' is extorting Klue and threatening to leak stolen data. Hallmarks resemble prior Salesforce token-theft extortion campaigns.

incidents.victim: Okendo Reviews (18,000+ online stores)
incidents.vector: Threat actor compromised the Okendo product-review widget and injected JavaScript delivering a 'ClickFix' lure that tricked visitors into pasting malicious commands into their terminal.
incidents.impact: More than 18,000 online stores were served the malicious widget, tied to an actor known for infostealer and RAT campaigns. The widget was restored to a safe version on May 14.

incidents.victim: Texas Republican Party
incidents.vector: Defendant hacked the party's web hosting account in 2021.
incidents.impact: A Canadian man pleaded guilty to hacking the Texas Republican Party website in 2021.

incidents.victim: Check Point Remote Access VPN customers worldwide
incidents.vector: Exploitation of CVE-2026-50751, a CVSS 9.3 authentication-bypass (certificate-validation flaw triggered when IKEv1 is enabled) allowing a fully authenticated VPN session without a password.
incidents.impact: A Qilin ransomware affiliate exploited the flaw from early May — about six weeks before disclosure — to compromise a few dozen organizations worldwide, using Rclone for exfiltration. CISA issued an emergency directive on June 21.

incidents.victim: Brazil national emergency alert system (Defesa Civil Nacional)
incidents.vector: Attacker gained access to the national alert system and pushed a false 'extreme-level' alert.
incidents.impact: A fake extreme alert was pushed to mobile phones across five regions including São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro and Brasília; the government took the system offline.

incidents.victim: Texas Parks and Wildlife Department
incidents.vector: Hackers accessed data of people who registered for hunting and fishing licenses on the agency's website.
incidents.impact: Personal details of more than 3 million people stolen, including government IDs, driver's licenses and home addresses.

incidents.victim: Kodak (customers)
incidents.vector: A data-extortion group listed Kodak on its dark-web leak portal claiming theft of customer records.
incidents.impact: The group claims to have stolen details of nearly 2.2 million customers; Kodak confirmed unauthorized access to its network.

incidents.victim: SocGolish malware operation (law enforcement takedown)
incidents.vector: SocGolish hijacked traffic from compromised websites to redirect users to scams, phishing and malware download pages.
incidents.impact: A Europol-led Operation Endgame phase seized 106 servers and domains; Dutch police removed the SocGolish backdoor from nearly 15,000 infected WordPress sites.

incidents.victim: Consumers with Android TV boxes and data-scraping targets
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — proxy and ad-fraud operation
incidents.vector: A malicious SDK pre-installed or bundled on unofficial Android TV boxes enrolls them into a residential proxy network.
incidents.impact: Millions of consumer TV boxes forced to relay traffic for ad fraud, account takeovers and mass data scraping; one May 2026 scraping event spanned more than 1.4 million IPs. Researchers link the proxy network to a publicly traded Israeli firm, which disputes the findings.

incidents.victim: Silver Fox cybercrime group (China arrests)
incidents.vector: The group ran malspam campaigns and fake download sites delivering a trojan that deployed infostealers and custom RATs to steal victims' assets.
incidents.impact: Chinese police arrested 67 suspects across five provinces, including the malware author; the group had primarily targeted Chinese-speaking users before expanding abroad.

incidents.victim: North American academic, medical and military research institutions
incidents.vector: Actor exploited externally facing REDCap research servers, deployed custom 'INFINITERED' malware to harvest legitimate login credentials, then pivoted to internal networks and abused Google Workspace content-compliance rules to silently BCC-forward sensitive email.
incidents.impact: A PRC-nexus actor remained undetected for over a year (earliest compromise September 2023), targeting research on AI, uncrewed systems, cyber programs, national defense and medicine across multiple US and Canadian institutions. Google disrupted the infrastructure and notified victims.

incidents.victim: Four major Iranian banks (Bank Melli, Bank Tejarat, Bank Saderat, Export Development Bank of Iran)
incidents.vector: Cyberattack targeting communications infrastructure shared by the four banks.
incidents.impact: Online portals and mobile apps for four of Iran's largest banks were down over a weekend; the banking council said no customer data was accessed. Intelligence sources believe Israeli hackers were likely responsible.
